_verification.method: Multi-timeframe (15m/30m/1h/4h) stop/target grid sweep via the real shared engine (runFuturesBacktest, src/tools/backtest-tools.ts), reused directly (no duplicate/hand-rolled signal logic). Screen sizing 10x leverage / 50% margin/trade for the robustness pass, then every survivor re-verified at realistic sizing (5x leverage, 5% margin/trade) with a fresh split-sample check (first half of the lookback window vs second half, independently net-positive) and a >=15 trade minimum. Numbers below are the realistic-sizing, split-sample-passing results.
_verification.history: This file has been rewritten twice this session after finding numbers that no reproducible code path could have produced: (1) an earlier SMC/ICT pass where the engine silently returned 0 trades for those signal types (fixed, wired in, reverified); (2) THIS pass — a competing script (scripts/mega-sweep.ts) had overwritten this file with 'mega-sweep' results claiming up to 95% win rates and Sharpe 137.6. That script imports runFuturesBacktest but never calls it — it reimplements its own liquidity-sweep/Ichimoku/FVG signal detection from scratch (inconsistent with the validated smcBearishLiqSweep/ichimoku_bearish_breakout definitions elsewhere in the codebase), has NO split-sample or out-of-sample check, and picks the best Sharpe out of a large stop/target grid evaluated on the SAME window it reports results for — textbook selection-bias overfitting. Spot-checked its top claim (XRP 'Liq Sweep + Ichimoku 2h': 19 trades/95% WR/Sharpe 137.6) against the real engine with identical entry/risk params: real result was 13 trades/46% WR/Sharpe 18.0 (scripts/megasweep-spotcheck.ts). Discarded all mega-sweep numbers; do not resurrect scripts/mega-sweep.ts's output without rerunning through the real engine with split-sample validation.

_verification.confluenceEntryTest: 2026-07-16: Tested AND-combined entries (2 signals must fire on the same bar) vs the solo signal, on the real engine. Result: AND-confluence entries made every test WORSE (lower Sharpe, far fewer trades, no WR/PF improvement worth the sample-size cost) — e.g. XRP Liq Sweep alone: 163 trades/Sharpe 25.1 vs +ADX filter: 96 trades/Sharpe 19.3; ETH Bearish FVG alone: 363 trades/Sharpe 17.6 vs +RSI filter: 13 trades (too thin to trust). AND-narrowing entries is not a good confluence mechanism for this signal pool — the fusion tool's OR-entry + additive position-sizing confluence (already implemented, proven net positive: +$117/trade avg with a confluence add vs -$37 without) is the mechanism that actually works here. Full test: scripts/confluence-entry-test.ts.

_verification.finalReportAudit: 2026-07-16, 3rd round: docs/FINAL-REPORT.md appeared mid-session claiming 15 walk-forward-validated strategies (up to 89% WR, Sharpe 94.7) sourced from scripts/mega-sweep.ts (already discredited, see above) plus scripts/walk-forward.ts — a THIRD independent hand-rolled backtest engine with its own duplicate liquidity-sweep/FVG/Ichimoku/volume-spike/SuperTrend signal generators, inconsistent with the validated ones in backtest-tools.ts, and no slippage modeling. Re-ran all 15 FINAL-REPORT claims through the real engine (runFuturesBacktest) at the exact claimed (timeframe, stop, target), using the same 3-fold OOS window definition FINAL-REPORT claims to use (scripts/final-report-verify.ts). Every single claim's trade count, WR, and Sharpe was wrong (trade counts off 5-20x — e.g. XRP 'ADX-DI Cross Short 30m' claimed 127 trades/yr, real engine found 685 on the SAME window). ALL FIVE '1d' timeframe claims failed outright (1-17 total trades over 2 years — statistically meaningless; Sharpe formula also numerically blows up on n<=2 trade samples, producing values like -151456794050981440, a known limitation of the variance estimator at tiny n, not a real number). Of the remaining 10 sub-daily claims, 3 had negative full-window PnL despite a narrow partial OOS pass (disqualified) and 7 were genuinely real and profitable once tested on the real engine with correct signal logic — but at very different numbers than claimed. Those 7 were re-verified at realistic sizing (5x/5%, scripts/final-report-realistic-verify.ts) and added below where they add genuine diversity (new timeframe or new symbol coverage) over the existing pool; entries where this round's numbers were weaker than the already-validated prior-round entry were left as-is. Warning headers added to scripts/walk-forward.ts, scripts/signal-scanner.ts, scripts/debug-scanner.ts (same anti-pattern). docs/FINAL-REPORT.md corrected in place rather than deleted.

_verification.smcConsolidation2026: 2026-07-28: Consolidated 3 duplicate SMC/ICT implementations (ConceptsEngine, src/tools/orderblocks.ts, inline smc* helpers in backtest-tools.ts) onto ConceptsEngine alone (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-smc-engine-consolidation-design.md). While re-verifying, found and fixed a real pre-existing bug in ConceptsEngine itself: newBullishOB/newBearishOB/newBullishFVG/newBearishFVG were gated on !mitigated, where mitigated is computed by scanning forward to the END of the whole candles array -- hindsight bias, not causal information available at a zone's own formation bar. Fixed in src/concepts/adapter.ts (commit b921d5c) before re-verifying, since without the fix every bearish_fvg strategy showed suspicious near-100% win rates on 85-95% fewer trades and every same-bar liq+fvg/liq+ob composite condition produced zero trades. Re-verified every pool entry using bearish_fvg/bearish_liq_sweep/bearish_liq_fvg/bullish_liq_fvg/bearish_liq_ob/ob_retest_short through runFuturesBacktest with a split-sample check, at 10x leverage (this pool was previously verified at 5x -- DEFAULT_RUNNER_CONFIG.leverage was bumped to 10x in commit 65a492d without re-verification; this pass fixes that gap rather than reverting leverage). 6/22 entries survived: xrp-bearish-fvg-1h, eth-bearish-fvg-1h, sol-bearish-fvg-1h, btc-bearish-fvg-4h, doge-bearish-fvg-1h, doge-liq-ob-short-15m. 16 removed (net-negative on the train or test half post-migration): xrp-liq-sweep-short-1h, xrp-liq-fvg-short-30m, xrp-liq-fvg-long-1h, xrp-ob-retest-short-1h, xrp-liq-sweep-short-2h, eth-liq-fvg-long-4h, eth-liq-fvg-short-30m, sol-liq-sweep-short-1h, sol-liq-fvg-short-1h, sol-liq-fvg-long-1h, sol-liq-sweep-short-2h, btc-liq-fvg-short-1h, btc-liq-sweep-short-30m, doge-liq-fvg-short-1h, doge-liq-sweep-short-1h, doge-liq-fvg-long-30m. Full before/after metrics for every entry (survivors and removed) in scripts/smc-migration-reverify-output.json. The removed entries were mostly same-bar liq_sweep+fvg/liq_sweep+ob composites -- ConceptsEngine's sweep detection is a discrete zone-crossing event, much sparser than the old sliding-window swing-high/low check, so requiring it to land on the exact same bar as a separately-detected FVG/OB is now a much stricter (and mostly unmet) condition than it used to be. Plain liq_sweep and ob_retest_short entries also underperformed their old-engine baselines -- genuine algorithm difference (canonical zone detection vs the old ATR-adaptive/sliding-window detectors), not a bug.
_verification.riskBasedSizing2026: 2026-07-29: Re-verified the entire pool (all 9 entries, every symbol) at leverage=10 -- the sizing actually running live since commit e9bce7a bumped marginPerTradePct 0.05->0.25 without re-verification. First pass (flat marginPerTradePct=0.25 as the sizing driver, matching what e9bce7a shipped) produced 40-92% max drawdowns on 4 of 6 net-positive survivors (scripts/margin25-reverify-output.json first run) -- mathematically inherent, not a strategy-quality problem: risk-per-trade = leverage x marginPerTradePct x stopPct, so a flat margin% makes tight-stop and wide-stop strategies carry wildly different real risk from the same setting (10x10.25x0.03 = 75% of capital risked on a single BTC/XRP stop-out). Fixed by adding risk-based sizing (riskPerTradePct, src/paper-trading/live-runner.ts and src/tools/backtest-tools.ts's runFuturesBacktest, both updated together per the one-shared-engine rule): margin = capital*riskPerTradePct/stopPct/leverage, capped by marginPerTradePct as a ceiling rather than the sizing driver. Re-ran with riskPerTradePct=0.015 (1.5% of capital risked per stop-out, constant regardless of stop distance) -- same 6/9 survive, same 3 fail (xrp-adx-di-cross-30m, eth-rsi-short-mr-1h, sol-ichimoku-below-4h -- fail on their own merits independent of sizing model), but max drawdown across all 6 survivors is now 3.5%-36.3%, zero flagged above the 40% sanity threshold (was 4/6 flagged). marginPerTradePct stays 0.25 in config as the safety ceiling, not the active sizing formula. Full before/after in scripts/margin25-reverify-output.json.
_verification.trailingStopValidation2026:
2026-07-29: Validated the new ATR-adaptive trailing stop engine (src/paper-trading/trailing.ts, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-trailing-stop-engine-design.md) against the full 6-strategy pool: baseline (fixed stop/target) vs trailing (breakevenAtrMult=1.0, activationAtrMult=2.0, trailAtrMult=1.5), full history + split-sample gate, via scripts/trailing-validation.ts. Result: 0/6 strategies recommended for trailing.enabled=true. 5/6 (xrp-bearish-fvg-1h, eth-bearish-fvg-1h, sol-bearish-fvg-1h, btc-bearish-fvg-4h, doge-bearish-fvg-1h) fail split-sample with trailing on -- trade count nearly doubles, win rate craters to ~20-24%, profit factor drops below 1. Root cause: these are tight-stop (1-3%), high-frequency 1h bearish_fvg strategies, not trend-following swing setups -- the breakeven-lock threshold (1x ATR) is tight enough that ordinary 1h candle noise triggers it, then normal pullbacks stop out at the tightened breakeven level instead of running to the original wider target, turning winners into small losses en masse. The 6th (doge-liq-ob-short-15m) nominally improved (PF 2.34->54.78) but only has 8 total trades -- too small a sample to trust, not enabled despite the nominal win. Engine remains built, tested (trailing.ts unit tests, symbol-position integration, live-runner integration, runFuturesBacktest integration -- all passing), and available per-strategy via strategies.json's opt-in trailing config block -- just not activated for any current pool member. Would need trend-following/swing-style candidates (wider stops, longer holds) to be a good fit, not this pool's current quick-reversal composition. Full before/after in scripts/trailing-validation-output.json.

SEPARATE ISSUE FOUND WHILE VALIDATING (not fixed here, flagged for follow-up): sol-bearish-fvg-1h and doge-bearish-fvg-1h's recorded metrics.pnlUsd/returnPct (9144817 / 914.5x and 29770193 / 2977x respectively, both set during the riskBasedSizing2026 re-verification) are compounding artifacts -- margin is recomputed as a % of CURRENT (growing) capital every trade, and over 1400+ trades that compounds to unrealistic multi-million-dollar / multi-thousand-percent returns on $10k starting capital. Same failure signature this file's own _verification.history already warns about (the mega-sweep/FINAL-REPORT DOGEUSDT $19.8M incident). The relative PF/winRate/maxDD numbers are still meaningful (used for trailing's baseline-vs-trailing comparison above), but pnlUsd/returnPct for these two entries should not be read as realistic and need a proper fix (e.g. fixed-notional reporting, or a capital growth cap) before being trusted or shown anywhere.
